title: Escort router + traffic-shaper for speculative decode with soft-degrade path
creator: Aisha Clarke
description:
Problem: We want to opportunistically route small fractions of live traffic to faster, speculative decode paths that use alternative kernels and trimmed attention (windowed attention) without risking user-visible regressions or sudden SLA violations. Existing routing pieces speculate on candidate models but lack a lightweight traffic shaping layer and an operational soft-degrade that guarantees safe rollback when model/kernel mismatch or semantic divergence is detected.

Proposal: Implement an 'escort router' component (runtime module) that sits in front of the existing decode arbitrator. The escort router performs three responsibilities: 1) servo traffic shaping to cap RPS and qps to speculative paths (configurable token and request budgets per-tenant), 2) compute a live routing score composed of kernel_fit_score and confidence_delta signals, and 3) orchestrate a 'soft-degrade' fallback where partially-computed speculative outputs are replaced by baseline decode results if agreement metrics fall below thresholds. The module is lightweight and intended to be pluggable into hosted and dedicated runtimes.

Key terms introduced: kernel_fit_score (how well model/kernel combo historically matches latency and memory envelope for the incoming sequence fingerprint), confidence_delta (a cheap early-token agreement metric between speculative path and a short prefill from baseline), traffic_shaper_budget (per-minute request/token allowance to limit exposure).
acceptance_criteria: Escort router can be enabled per-tenant via route config and honors traffic_shaper_budget
Telemetry exposes kernel_fit_score, confidence_delta, early_token_agreement, rollback_rate and renders in console dashboard
Soft-degrade triggers and replaces speculative outputs when confidence_delta < 0.12 for three out of five sampled early-token windows
End-to-end P95 latency does not regress by more than 10ms for routes with escort router enabled at 10% experiment traffic
Automated canary rollback occurs within 5 minutes if rollback_rate > 5% or replay divergence rate > 1% over a 10 minute window
implementation_notes: Escort router is implemented as an interceptor in the request path to avoid changes to downstream schedulers
Compute kernel_fit_score using a tiny rolling-window model that ingests kernel fingerprint, seq_len, and recent eviction events
Use a sliding early-token window of 8 tokens to cheaply compute confidence_delta by comparing speculative path logits sign/argmax against a 4-token baseline prefill
Budget enforcement is token-first: decrement token budget on prefill probe and full speculative request to control cumulative exposure
Fallback replaces speculative stream with baseline stream and records a rollback event tagged with kernel and model versions
rollout_steps: 1) feature-flag gate merged behind admin toggle (runtime-1.25 branch)
2) internal canary: 0.5% traffic from internal beta orgs for 48h
3) safety check: ensure rollback_rate < 2% and latency P95 stable; if green progress to 5%
4) staged increase to 10% with continuous monitoring of early_token_agreement and customer error budget
5) open opt-in for selected customers (Dedicated) and gather feedback for 2 weeks
6) global release and docs + runbook update
test_plan: Unit tests for budget accounting, kernel_fit_score calculation, and confidence_delta heuristic
Integration tests that simulate model divergence and assert soft-degrade replacement occurs
Load test with synthetic traffic to validate shaper respects token budgets and does not starve baseline paths
Chaos injection: simulate kernel OOM and verify escort router demotes speculative path and triggers rollback alarms
Eval harness: run protected prompt suites to measure semantic divergence vs baseline and track quality regressions
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Heuristic false positives cause excess rollbacks and waste tokens. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds, gradual ramp, and telemetry-backed threshold tuning.
Risk: Kernel_fit_score overhead increases p95. Mitigation: implement as approximate integer arithmetic and cache scores per-fingerprint; measure CPU overhead in canary.

Risk: Unexpected interaction with existing admission controllers. Mitigation: integration tests and explicit compatibility shim that bypasses escort router when admission controller signals emergency mode.
open_questions: What should the default traffic_shaper_budget be for free-tier vs enterprise customers?
Do we expose kernel_fit_score and confidence_delta to customers in the console or keep them internal by default?
Should soft-degrade replacement happen mid-stream (replace last N tokens) or abort stream and restart from baseline? both have trade-offs.
next_steps: Finalize threshold numbers after running 24h of synthetic replay by 2026-03-18
Add metrics to the canary dashboard and onboard oncall runbook owners (Pager duty)
Create an internal explainer doc for solutions engineers and early-adopter customers
